turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your impertinence is matched only by your ignorance, Sandip. The safety of your own people, not to mention the law, demands that you desist from these oppressive tactics.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip-da, perhaps we should listen to what Nikhil-da has to say. His concerns seem genuine, don't you think?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: If the law demands it, why do I see your own villagers trembling at the mere mention of your name? Ask them, they'll tell you the story of how their sons are taken from their homes, never to be seen again.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be lectured by you on the loyalty of my villagers, Sandip. I will speak to them myself, and I assure you, they will tell you the same truth: that your influence is the one that drives them to fear.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And I'm sure they'd also tell you about your... 'generosity' in extracting taxes from them, leaving them with barely enough to eat. Tell me, Nikhil, how do you reconcile your zeal for the law with your own brand of justice?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your baseless accusations, Sandip. The taxes I collect are for the welfare of my villagers, and I will not be lectured by one who has brought nothing but chaos to this region.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil-da, still relying on the classic 'I'm a just collector' routine, I see. Tell me, have you considered a career in comedy? Your act is getting stale.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, for the last time: the Mussulmans are not to be underestimated. Their leader, Hakim Khan, has been making overtures towards me, and I will not be caught off guard.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, so now Hakim Khan is playing the big shot, is he? I'm sure it's not just a clever ploy to get more land from you, Nikhil.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in your petty banter, Sandip, but I implore you to take this threat seriously. The safety of our villagers is at stake, and I will not be deterred from protecting them.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil-da, still trying to play the hero, are you? I'm sure the villagers are just fascinated by your tales of bravery.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have done nothing but warn you, Sandip, and yet you persist in mocking me. The time for jests is over; it is time to take action.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what action would you have me take, Nikhil-da? Ride off into battle, with my poet's quill and my noble steed?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your flippant remarks, Sandip. I will ride to the village of Hakim Khan myself, to assess the situation and ensure the villagers' safety.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You'd do well to ride into the jaws of hell itself, Nikhil-da, but I suppose that's not your style. I'll have my men handle the situation, thank you very much.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your men will be of little use against the Mussulmans, Sandip. I warn you, they will not hesitate to attack if provoked.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what's to stop them from attacking, eh? The majesty of my estate, perhaps, or the brilliance of my poetry?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala, please see to it that our stores are prepared for any contingency. We must not be caught off guard if the situation escalates.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip-da, perhaps it would be wise to listen to Nikhil-da's warnings, as he has experience in such matters.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You think you're a great strategist, Nikhil-da, but your tactics are as dull as your poetry. I'll not be cowed by empty threats and self-important warnings.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
